# decode_string_array_runtime fixtures

Real `javascript-obfuscator` output built from one `source.js` (24 distinct string literals), so
"decoded" can be asserted as: every string of the source is in the dump.

| File | Generated by | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| `source.js` | nothing (not obfuscated) | exit 1, `string array not found` |
| `obfuscator-0.27.4-plain-strings.js` | 0.27.4, plain string table | decoded, array at the top level (`wrapper: null`) |
| `obfuscator-2.19.1-plain-strings.js` | 2.19.1 | decoded, array wrapped in a table function |
| `obfuscator-4.1.1-plain-strings.js` | 4.1.1 | decoded |
| `obfuscator-5.10.1-plain-strings.js` | 5.10.1 | decoded |
| `obfuscator-2.19.1-base64.js` | 2.19.1, base64 strings | decoded, each value with its `(raw: …)` companion |
| `obfuscator-4.1.1-base64.js` | 4.1.1 | decoded |
| `obfuscator-5.10.1-base64.js` | 5.10.1 | decoded |
| `obfuscator-2.19.1-rc4.js` | 2.19.1: rc4 + rotation + shuffle + flattening + dead code + self-defending | **refused**: `rc4 string table`, nothing printed |
| `obfuscator-5.10.1-rc4.js` | 5.10.1, same hardened config | **refused** |

These did not exist before v1.8.5. The tool's only tests ran hand-written samples that happened to
fit what it looked for, and on every real output it decoded nothing — see the cases in
`tests/unit/decode-string-array-runtime-samples.test.js`.

Not in the set, on purpose: a table that sits inside the program's own wrapper IIFE (the live
127 KB bundle this was first tried on cannot be published). The tool refuses to run such a file;
the test builds one on the fly from `source.js`.

## Regenerating

```
npx javascript-obfuscator@4.1.1 source.js --config obfuscator.config.plain-table.json --output obfuscator-4.1.1-plain-strings.js
```

with `obfuscator.config.base64.json` and `obfuscator.config.rc4-hardened.json` for the other two
rows. Output is random (names, order, rotation), so regenerated files differ byte for byte while
asserting the same things.
